ratings.reviewer_notes: Human DMD study documents systemic IL-1, TNF-alpha, IL-6, and CRP patterns in relation to muscle function and nutritional status, but it is primarily associative and does not establish a mechanism sustaining chronic inflammation.

Directly identifies CCR2-dependent recruitment of inflammatory Ly6C-high monocytes and proinflammatory macrophage skewing as drivers of inflammation and pathology in mdx muscle; genetic and pharmacological inhibition improves outcomes.

Direct mechanistic evidence that fibrin deposition after muscle-vascular damage sustains leukocyte alphaMbeta2-integrin-mediated inflammatory programs, degeneration, and impaired regeneration in dystrophic muscle.

Green tea extract reduces mdx pathology and NF-kappaB staining, supporting NF-kappaB as an inflammation-associated pathway, but the intervention study does not clearly establish how DMD initiates or sustains chronic inflammation.

Quercetin lowers NF-kappaB-related proteins, COX-2, TGF-beta1, and macrophage marker F4/80 in mdx hearts. This is useful intervention-based support for inflammatory pathways but provides indirect mechanistic evidence.

Focused review directly describes neutrophil mechanisms that may prolong DMD inflammation, including proinflammatory cytokines, myeloperoxidase, neutrophil elastase, oxidative stress, worsened muscle damage, and impaired regeneration.

Shows that connexin hemichannels contribute to sarcolemmal permeability, calcium elevation, NF-kappaB activation, apoptosis, and necrosis in mdx myofibers. This supports an upstream damage/NF-kappaB segment, although macrophage infiltration was unchanged.

Human DMD muscle study directly characterizes persistent inflammatory and oxidative pathways, including NF-kappaB activation and increased TNF-alpha, IL-6, and glutathione peroxidase, and relates them to age, necrosis, and regeneration.

Provides direct causal evidence that persistent IKK/NF-kappaB signaling in macrophages promotes inflammation and necrosis, while signaling in myofibers limits progenitor-mediated regeneration; genetic and pharmacological inhibition improves mdx pathology.

Focused review connects dystrophin loss and repeated myonecrosis to associated inflammation and oxidative damage, with particular attention to neutrophils and protein thiol oxidation. It supplies directly relevant mechanism-level context.
